title: AGENT7 emissions are permanently disabled beyond Genesis Supply and Launch Agent 7 Governance cannot revert it
content:
A.6.1.1.8.2.1.4.2.1.1.6 states that "Token emissions beyond the Genesis Supply are permanently disabled; this cannot be reverted by Launch Agent 7 Governance."

The operative clause is the second half. Disabling emissions is unremarkable; disabling the *power to re-enable* them is the actual commitment. It removes dilution from the Agent's own decision space, which means AGENT7 holders do not have to trust, monitor, or vote against their issuer to be protected from inflation.

This is a deliberate self-binding move: the Agent gives up an instrument it might later want. The value it buys is that the fixed supply becomes verifiable from the Artifact rather than contingent on future governance composition — no future majority of Agent voters can be assembled to change it.

The cost is loss of flexibility precisely when flexibility would be most tempting: an Agent in distress cannot mint its way out. The Atlas accepts that cost at the Agent level and relocates the emergency lever to a higher authority instead (see the Sky Governance carve-out in the same section).
description: The Agent's own governance is denied the mint switch as a written parameter, making fixed supply a structural property of the token rather than a standing promise by its issuer.
